messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a sensitivity scan for per-layer quant on stable-7b with embeddings + lm_head excluded and saw a ~12% p99 latency regression under realistic batch mixes. anyone seen this pattern before?
jeremy: can you paste the exact config? might be a kernel selection flip or kv-cache churn.
maya: here is the run config i used:
```json
{
  "model": "stable-7b",
  "quant_mode": "per_layer",
  "exclude_layers": ["embedding", "lm_head"],
  "calibration": "layerwise_ema",
  "kernel_autotune": true,
  "batching": {"max_batch": 64, "dynamic": true, "bucket_by_seq": true},
  "kv_cache_policy": "reuse_if_prefix"
}
```
sasha: i ran a short profile on the same config — kernel_selector is oscillating between int8 and fp8 kernels in mid layers (layers 7-10) for many requests. that causes extra kernel-switch overhead + extra memcpy on the KV hot path.
alex: we see same on perf traces: memcpy on kv_path up ~18% and kernel-launchs up ~22% when the selector flips frequently. token/s dropped ~7% overall, p99 went from ~120ms -> 135ms.
eva: that could be calibration-induced scale variance. per-layer quant with embedding/lm_head excluded changes the layer index mapping used during scale table lookups. if the selector uses layer idxs for heuristic lookups, it might query the wrong profile and pick a suboptimal kernel.
jeremy: good call. i remember a previous bug where the excluded-layer mask wasn't applied when building the kernel_profile array — leaving a stale alignment.
maya: reproduction command i used: `./bench --model stable-7b --seq 512 --batch 8 --profile --quant=per_layer --exclude embedding,lm_head --kv on`
sasha: sample profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[profile] layer=6 kernel=int8 time=1.2ms
[profile] layer=7 kernel=fp8  time=2.6ms  // fallback observed
[profile] kv memcpy bytes=12MB count=160 time=3.1ms
[profile] layer=8 kernel=int8 time=1.1ms
[profile] layer=9 kernel=fp8  time=2.7ms
```
alex: that alternating fp8 spikes exactly where kernel selector index differs when exclusions are present.
jeremy: quick triage steps i suggest:
• add unit that simulates exclude mask and ensures kernel_profile alignment
• run sensitivity sweep with varied batch distributions (many small vs few large)
• add hysteresis to kernel selection so it doesn't flip on single-sample noise
maya: adding to my todo. i'll own the unit test and a small canary run.
eva: in parallel i can run a calibration-vs-runtime test: same calibration output but force kernel selection to use per-model static profile to compare. helps separate calibration noise vs selector bug.
sasha: also watch kv cache eviction heuristics — when kernel switches to a slower path we saw requests stall and occasionally reallocate kv buffers which amplifies tail. maybe the selector should prefer kernels that preserve kv layout.
jeremy: agree. for now, a pragmatic short-term fix is to prefer kernels with identical kv layout and add a stickiness window of n tokens. longer term we can add cost-model that includes memcpy + kernel time.
maya: noted. i'll patch the selector to add simple stickiness (3 requests) and run overnight canary with mixed batch generator.
alex: patched locally and ran 1000-request synthetic mix: p99 -> baseline+1.5% (vs +12% before). promising. sharing diff in PR shortly.
maya: great — i will also add a regression test that reproduces the exact mixed-batch distribution that triggered the regression.
jeremy: can we also add a small telemetry flag to log when kernel selection changes for a layer (so ops-team can spot thrash in prod)? low-overhead sampling only.
eva: +1, sampling every 0.5% of requests should be fine.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 02:00 UTC with tag `pr/quant-selector-stickiness` — notify #eng-runtime if anything spikes. :rocket: 
maya: thanks all — summary: unit test for exclude-mask alignment, selector stickiness patch, calibration forced-profile A/B, telemetry sampling. i'll post results by EOD. :thumbsup:
